ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In the circuits shown in A and B, the resistance values of resistor R and self-induction coil L are both very small, and are smaller than the resistance of bulb A. Close S, so that the circuit reaches stability, and bulb A lights up. Then (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.title: Figure Jia open-ended question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: In the circuit shown in Jia, after closing S to make the circuit reach steady state and bulb A light up, then opening S, how will bulb A change?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In the circuit shown in Jia, after closing S to make the circuit reach steady state and bulb A light up, then opening S, how will bulb A change?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached circuit diagram contains two figures, Jia and Yi; the question only asks about Figure Jia. In Figure Jia, the left and right sides are common nodes; the upper branch, from left to right, is bulb A and self-induction coil L in sequence; the middle branch is resistor R, connecting the left and right nodes; the lower branch is power supply E and switch S. That is to say, after S is opened, the power supply branch is disconnected, but A and L in the upper branch and R in the middle branch can still form a closed loop through the left and right nodes. Reasoning: When S is closed and steady state is reached, there is already a steady current in the A-L branch where bulb A is located, so A lights up. At the instant S is opened again, the power supply branch is cut off, but the current in self-induction coil L cannot change suddenly. It will produce a self-induced electromotive force to maintain the original branch current, causing the current to continue through the closed loop formed by bulb A, coil L, and resistor R. Afterwards, the magnetic field energy stored in the coil is gradually transformed and consumed in the bulb and resistor, and the loop current gradually decreases, so the brightness of bulb A gradually weakens.
